_readme: Monitoring configuration for the sensor-based water quality indicator. Every value here is configurable. Reference ranges are DEFAULTS taken from commonly cited drinking-water aesthetic/operational references; they are NOT Qatari regulatory limits and have NOT been confirmed by any authority. Set 'confirmed' to true only after the responsible institution has approved them. A null range means 'no threshold configured': that parameter is displayed but not classified.

operations._readme: refreshSeconds: the dashboard asks the database for new rows this often (only rows it has not seen yet). fullReloadSeconds: a complete reload, to drop rows that aged out. useLastKnownValues: true = the dashboard always shows each sensor's latest valid reading however old, labelled 'Last known value' when older than freshnessMinutes; false = such readings are excluded. freshnessMinutes: a device whose newest reading is older than this is shown as offline (set it to a few multiples of the devices' real reporting interval). deviceLookbackHours: devices with no reading in this window are not listed at all.

validity._readme: Physical plausibility filters (not quality thresholds). A value outside these bounds is treated as a sensor fault and ignored, never as zero.

ph.label: pH
ph.source: Default reference range 6.5-8.5: US EPA National Secondary Drinking Water Regulations (aesthetic) and the range commonly cited by WHO for operational control. WHO sets no health-based guideline value for pH. neutralBand is a display convention for the Acidic / Neutral / Alkaline label only.
ph.criticalSource: Critical below 6.0 or above 9.0 (added 14 Nov): well outside FAO 29's normal range for irrigation water (6.5-8.4); strongly acidic or alkaline water needs action.

temperature.label: Water temperature
temperature.source: AquaMaa operational band for well water in Qatar (15-35 °C; above 40 °C treated as critical: a sensor fault or water heated at the surface). There is no universal regulatory limit for water temperature: replace with the responsible institution's site-specific range.

tds_ppm.label: Total dissolved solids
tds_ppm.source: Default upper reference 1000 mg/L (~ppm): WHO background document on TDS in drinking-water (taste acceptability; no health-based guideline value). US EPA secondary standard is stricter (500 mg/L). Replace with the limit that applies to the intended use of each well.
tds_ppm.criticalSource: Critical above 2000 mg/L (added 14 Nov): FAO 29 severe restriction on use for irrigation.

turbidity_index.label: Turbidity
turbidity_index.source: Turbidity index computed on the ESP32 from the turbidity sensor (0 = clear water); the device also sends a status (turbidity_status). Not NTU: no NTU conversion has been validated. No limit is configured, so it is shown, not assessed; the device's status and the unusual-change check raise its alerts.

aggregation._readme: How values are combined. The dashboard takes the latest valid reading of each device, combines the devices of the same well ('withinWell'), then combines the wells ('acrossWells'). Methods: mean | median | hydrogenMean (pH only: mean of hydrogen-ion activity, the chemically correct way to average pH of the same water). pH uses the median across wells because a mean of different wells' pH has no chemical meaning; TDS uses the median because salinity is skewed and one saline well should not drag the headline; temperature uses the mean because it is linear with a narrow spread; raw turbidity uses the median because it is uncalibrated and spiky.

wqi._readme: CCME Water Quality Index (CCME 2001): WQI = 100 - sqrt(F1^2 + F2^2 + F3^2) / 1.732, with F1 = % of variables failing, F2 = % of tests failing, F3 = amplitude of the failures. Objectives are each parameter's 'reference' range above; a parameter with no reference is left out (and listed as left out). Turbidity is never included: it is a raw, uncalibrated reading. One test = one well value per time bucket of the selected period. Categories: Excellent 95-100, Good 80-94, Fair 65-79, Marginal 45-64, Poor 0-44. CCME recommends at least 4 variables and 4 samples; with fewer the index is shown as indicative. An alert is raised when a well's index falls into one of alertCategories (Poor is critical).

waterUse._readme: Water Card: what each well's water is good for, from its latest valid TDS (and pH for drinking). Crop limits are the salinity of irrigation water (ECw, dS/m) at which the crop still gives its full yield, FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Table 4, converted with TDS ≈ 640 × ECw (FAO 29). The same table is AquaMaa's fastpath/data/crop_tolerance.csv, so the dashboard, Pepper and the agent agree. Drinking is judged on taste only (WHO): it never says 'safe to drink', which needs a laboratory test. An alert is raised when a well's water is not suitable for one or more of these uses.

drinking.label: Drinking (taste)
drinking.source: WHO TDS background document (taste); pH 6.5-8.5 (US EPA secondary standard / WHO operational range)
drinking.note: Taste only: safety needs a laboratory test

waterUse.source: FAO 29 Table 4 (Ayers & Westcot 1985), via AquaMaa fastpath/data/crop_tolerance.csv (draft, Mais to check)

statusAlerts._readme: Alerts from the text statuses the ESP32 sends. normal: any other value raises an alert. alertOn: only these values raise one. critical: values that make it urgent. messages: the advice Pepper and Telegram add (by value, or '*'). Values are compared without case. Confirm the full list of values with the ESP32 code (Munira).

messages.*: The water is no longer clear: check for sediment, a disturbed well or a dirty probe before use.

messages.NO WATER: Check the well and the pump; if water is present, the probes may be out of the water, so the other readings may not be valid.
messages.*: The water level is low: avoid over-pumping and check the well.

deviation.method: Modified z-score of the current network median against the median of earlier time buckets in the selected period (Iglewicz & Hoaglin, 1993)
